title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Overview

Purpose
Redwood's people operations playbook describes the standardized process and guardrails for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. This document is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, recruiters, people-ops partners, and people leaders. It reduces ambiguity, improves candidate and new hire experience, and ensures equitable performance practices.

Scope
Applies to all full-time employees, contractors hired for long-term engagements (>6 months), and hiring teams across Engineering, Product, Go-to-Market, and Support. Exceptions (e.g., executive hires, acquisitions) are noted in the Deviations section.

Key principles
- Candidate experience first: timely communications and transparent timelines.
- Hire for impact: role clarity, competencies, and job scorecards drive decisions.
- Manager enablement: managers are accountable for onboarding outcomes and performance conversations.
- Equity and consistency: structured interviews, rubrics, and calibration to reduce bias.

Roles and ownership (high level)
- Hiring Manager: defines role, approves final offer, owns onboarding plan and first 90 days.
- Recruiter: sources, screens, coordinates interviews, and owns offer logistics.
- Interviewers: evaluate against the job scorecard and submit feedback within 48 hours.
- People Ops: sets policy, supports offers, coordinates calibration, maintains templates.

Hiring process (standard flow)
1) Requisition & Scorecard (owned by Hiring Manager + Recruiter)
   - Create requisition in HRIS with job summary, required/desired skills, compensation band, and success criteria.
   - Attach a 1-page job scorecard that lists top 5 competencies and example measures of success.
   - Target SLA: requisition posted within 5 business days of hiring approval.

2) Sourcing & Screening (Recruiter)
   - Initial recruiter phone screen to confirm baseline skills, role fit, and compensation expectations. Aim for 20-30 minutes.
   - Recruiter to provide a candidate brief to the hiring manager after the screen.
   - Sourcing SLA target: first slate (3-5 qualified candidates) delivered within 14 calendar days of posting.

3) Interview loop (Hiring Manager + Interviewers)
   - Typical panel: 4-6 interviews covering technical skills, product sense (if applicable), systems thinking, and culture-add. Include at least one cross-functional interviewer.
   - Use structured interview rubrics; interviewers submit scores and narrative within 48 hours.
   - Interviewers must take training in structured interviewing (People Ops workshop or e-learning).

4) Decision & Offer (Hiring Manager + Recruiter + People Ops)
   - Hiring manager consolidates feedback and makes a decision within 72 hours of final interview.
   - People Ops must approve compensation band alignment before an offer is extended.
   - Offer turnaround goal: candidate receives verbal offer within 5 business days of decision. Written offer should follow within 2 business days.

5) Negotiation & Acceptance
   - Standard approach: recruiter leads negotiation with hiring manager guidance; People Ops supports approvals for exceptions.
   - Accepted offer should be countersigned and returned in the HRIS, and a start date confirmed within 3 business days.

Hiring metrics and targets
- Time-to-fill target: 35 calendar days (req approved -> candidate start).
- Offer acceptance rate target: >= 70%.
- Interview-to-offer ratio target: <= 6:1.
- Recruiter response SLA: initial outreach follow-up within 48 hours.

Interviewing standards and rubrics
- All interviews must be based on the job scorecard competencies.
- Interviewers complete a numeric rubric (1-5) and a short narrative. Rubric anchors are provided in the interview guide.
- At least two interviewers must independently rate a candidate as a 4 or 5 to extend an offer for senior IC roles; for manager roles, at least one peer and one people leader must provide a 4+.

Onboarding (30-60-90 framework)
Pre-boarding (Recruiter + IT + Manager)
- Send welcome email and new hire packet (HRIS onboarding tasks, benefits enrollment, paperwork) within 48 hours of signed offer.
- IT to provision laptop, network access, and required licenses at least 3 business days before start date. For remote hires, ship equipment to arrive 2 business days before first day.

First day
- Manager-run Welcome (60-90 min): team introductions, org overview, immediate priorities, and calendar of first-week meetings.
- People Ops orientation (30-45 min): benefits overview, payroll, policy highlights, and SLAs for questions.
- Schedule 1:1 weekly cadence set for first 90 days.

30-day goals (Onboarding success signals)
- Complete all required compliance training and security onboarding.
- Deliver a small ramp project or documentation update demonstrating core role competence.
- Manager to submit 30-day onboarding check-in in HRIS.

60-day goals
- Independent ownership of primary operational tasks; contribute to a team planning session.
- People Ops/Manager check-in to confirm access and role alignment.

90-day goals
- Demonstrated impact on at least one measurable outcome defined in the job scorecard.
- Manager completes 90-day review and confirms role fit or identifies development plan.

Onboarding checklist (example table)
Item | Owner | Due
--- | --- | ---
Welcome email + packet | Recruiter | Before start date
Equipment & access | IT | 3 days before start
First-week schedule | Manager | First day
Security & compliance training | Employee | Day 7
30/60/90 check-ins | Manager | Day 30 / 60 / 90

Performance & feedback cycle
Cadence and calendar
- Annual performance cycle: Goal setting in March, mid-year check-in in August, calibration and final ratings in December.
- Managers must complete written feedback and rating submission by the announced deadline (typically Dec 15).
- Mid-cycle calibration: all people managers participate in calibration meetings led by People Ops.

Goal-setting and OKRs
- Goals should be SMART, tied to team OKRs, and include quantitative success criteria where possible.
- Employees should draft goals with manager input during the March kickoff.

Continuous feedback and 1:1s
- Managers should hold weekly or bi-weekly 1:1s with direct reports. Agenda should include status, blockers, career development, and calibration with the job scorecard.
- Encourage immediate, specific feedback using the Red/Yellow/Green framing for risk.

Performance ratings and calibration
- Rating scale: 1 (Needs improvement), 2 (Meets expectations), 3 (Exceeds expectations), 4 (Outstanding).
- Managers must justify ratings with examples mapped to competencies and job scorecard outcomes.
- Calibration meetings align cross-functional expectations and identify promotion candidates or corrective development plans.

Promotion and leveling guidance
- Promotion packet (manager-owned) should include: updated job scorecard, 3-5 evidence bullets, peer feedback, and a proposed new level.
- People Ops runs a promotion committee monthly. Cut-off for packets is the 10th of the month for review that month.

Manager guide: day-to-day responsibilities
1) 1:1s and development
   - Hold regular 1:1s, prepare an agenda, set clear action items, and recap outcomes in the HRIS notes.
   - Use the career ladder rubric to coach towards the next level.
2) Performance conversations
   - Have timely check-ins for performance dips and document conversations. For performance improvement plans (PIPs), consult People Ops before initiating.
3) Hiring and onboarding
   - Partner with recruiter to finalize job scorecard and interview loop.
   - Own the first 90 days: set clear objectives and remove blockers.
4) Compensation and raises
   - Provide market context to People Ops when requesting salary exceptions. People Ops approves out-of-band offers or adjustments.
5) Offboarding
   - Conduct an exit conversation focusing on retention signals and handover; submit offboarding checklist at least 3 days before last day.

Templates and recommended language
- Interview decline template: a short, respectful note with encouragement to apply for future roles and an offer to provide feedback.
- Offer email template and standard benefits summary are available in the People Ops folder.

Deviations and approvals
- Executive hires, exceptions to compensation bands, and expedited timelines require VP People Ops approval.
- Document all deviations in the requisition notes and notify People Ops for audit purposes.

Accessibility and accommodations
- Redwood provides reasonable accommodations for candidates and employees. Request process: email accommodations@redwood.com or contact People Ops partner. Response SLA: 3 business days.

Metrics and continuous improvement
People Ops tracks: time-to-fill, acceptance rate, ramp time (30/60/90 outcomes), retention at 6/12 months, and diversity of slate metrics. Quarterly reviews of the hiring playbook occur with stakeholders.

FAQ (short)
Q: Who signs the offer?
A: People Ops reviews and approves; the hiring manager extends the offer via recruiter.

Q: What if an interviewer misses the feedback deadline?
A: Hiring manager should follow up immediately. If feedback is not received in 48 hours, People Ops will request completion or provide alternate evaluation.

Q: How do I request an exception to the compensation band?
A: Submit a compensation exception form to People Ops with market data and recommended rationale. People Ops will respond within 5 business days.
